All 118 episodes of Load-Bearing: the current series The Water Year, six episodes to start with and the full archive by year.
Meet the four people who make Load-Bearing in a former substation in Sheffield, how the show is funded and how to pitch an episode.
Follow Load-Bearing in your podcast app, get The Inspection Report by email every Friday, or join 2,140 members who pay for the show.

values.title: We make a show about the boring bits
values.text: Load-Bearing started as an argument in a pub about who is responsible for a wobbly footbridge. 118 episodes later we are still finding out. These are the rules we make it by.

principles.title: Go and stand next to it
principles.text: Every episode is recorded on site at least once. You can hear the pumps.

principles.title: Ask the night shift
principles.text: The person holding the torch knows more than the press office.

principles.title: No villains, only budgets
principles.text: Most failures are slow and shared. We explain them without a pile-on.

principles.title: Show the working
principles.text: Transcripts, sources and corrections for every episode, free.

values.eyebrow: The hosts, interviewed by each other
values.title: “Nobody posts a photo of a drain that worked”
values.intro: For episode 100 Ines and Tomasz swapped chairs and asked each other the questions listeners send most. This is a short extract.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why make a show about infrastructure at all? You had a perfectly good job.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Because I spent eleven years writing reports that three people read. A bridge I flagged in 2016 was closed in 2022 and everyone was surprised. I wanted to explain these things before the closure, not after.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People assume it is a show about disasters.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: It is the opposite. Nobody posts a photo of a drain that worked. We go and find the people who made it work, usually at four in the morning.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the one question you ask every guest?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: “What would you fix first if nobody had to approve it?” The answer is never the expensive thing. It is always a valve, a spreadsheet or a phone number.

values.title: A small, listener-funded operation
values.body:
Load-Bearing is made by four people in a converted 1950s substation in Kelham Island, Sheffield. We publish every Tuesday, with a break in August when the team goes outside.

About seven tenths of our income comes from 2,140 members. The rest comes from one sponsor per episode, chosen by us and always read by a host. Sponsors never see a script in advance.

values.title: Awards and other surprises
values.summary: Five awards in three years, all of them for episodes about things people walk past.

values.title: One sponsor per episode, read by a human
values.intro: We only take companies we would use ourselves, and no sponsor sees a script before it goes out. These are the ones paying for the 2026 season.

values.title: Know a pump, bridge or timetable we should cover?
values.text: The best episodes start with an email from someone who works there. Tell us what it is and why it matters. You do not need to be the boss, and we never name a source without asking.

steps.title: Callum reads it
steps.text: Every pitch gets a reply, including the ones we cannot make.

steps.title: A 20-minute call
steps.text: Ines or Tomasz rings to hear the story in your own words.

steps.title: We come to you
steps.text: We record on site, around your shift, and you hear the edit before it goes out.

values.title: Here’s what lands in your inbox on Friday
values.issueTitle: The valve nobody had turned since 1987
values.excerpt:
On Tuesday night Gareth from Pennine Water took us to a junction in Hillsborough and lifted a cover I must have walked over a thousand times. Underneath was a valve the size of a bin lid, last turned, according to the chalk on the chamber wall, in March 1987.

It still turned. That is the part that got me. Somebody greased it properly thirty-nine years ago, wrote the date on the wall and went home, and their work was still good on the night we needed it.

This week’s number is 2,900: the kilometres of water main under Sheffield alone. About a third of them were laid before 1920. Here is how Gareth decides which ones to listen to first.

values.title: Before you subscribe
values.intro: The things people ask most about listening, the Friday email and membership.

items.question: Is the show really free?
items.answer: Yes. Every episode, transcript and Friday email is free and always will be. Members pay so that it stays that way for everyone else.

items.question: What do members get that I don’t?
items.answer: A feed with no sponsor reads, two extended interviews a month and a members-only Q&A every quarter. Chief Engineers also come on two site visits a year.

items.question: Can I cancel a membership?
items.answer: In two clicks from any receipt email, with no questions and no exit survey. You keep access until the end of the month you paid for.

items.question: What do you do with my email address?
items.answer: We send you The Inspection Report on Fridays and nothing else. We never sell, share or rent the list, and every email has an unsubscribe link at the top.

items.question: Is there a transcript?
items.answer: Yes, with every episode on the day it comes out, checked by a human. If you spot a mistake, reply to any email and Callum will fix it.
